title: Transversality and the strong Whitney embedding theorem
summary: Transversality of a map to a submanifold (Definition 18.1); preimages of submanifolds; the parametric transversality theorems (18.3, 18.5, 18.8) deduced from Sard; the strong Whitney embedding theorem (Theorem 19.1): a compact n-manifold embeds in R^{2n}.

objectives.description: Prove the transverse-preimage theorem and the finite-dimensional parametric transversality theorem.
Explain the Fredholm parameter version and the meaning and limits of genericity.
Analyse transverse double points and distinguish the proved projection bound from the additional Whitney-trick input for the strong theorem.

preparation.description: Read lecture 20: §18 parametric transversality, Definition 18.1 and Theorems 18.3, 18.5, 18.8 with proofs.
Read lectures 21–22: §19 Theorem 19.1 (Whitney 1944) and the Whitney trick.

activities.title: Lecture and exact source reading
activities.instructions: Work through the prepared lecture together with its named source sections. Reconstruct the displayed derivations before looking back. The source reading is part of this unit, including the proof obligations identified in the notes.

activities.title: Problem sheet and discussion
activities.instructions: Write an independent attempt at each problem. Use one hint at a time if needed; preserve the original attempt and record what assistance changed. Explain the hypotheses aloud before requesting a step check.

activities.title: Return without the scaffolding
activities.instructions: After a gap, reconstruct the central argument without notes and revisit the transfer or synthesis problem. Compare against your previous work only afterwards. Record what remains unresolved; reading or recall alone does not certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to sample the listed objectives. Give an independent account of the main theorem and its hypotheses, and solve the transfer/synthesis task. An accepted single exercise is evidence only for its tested capabilities, not whole-unit mastery.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Transversality means two sets do not intersect.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It controls the tangent spaces when they meet. Transverse curves in a surface can cross.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Sard and a dimension count prove the strong Whitney embedding theorem by themselves.
commonMisconceptions.correction: They arrange controlled double points for an immersion. Removing those points requires the additional Whitney construction and its hypotheses.
